intended_object: The image of a subgroupoid S of C under a functor φ : C ⥤ D that is injective on objects, i.e. the subgroupoid of D whose arrows are the φ.map f with f ∈ S (inferred from the docstring and the name).
explanation: The arrows are defined by the inductive predicate Map.Arrows, whose only constructor puts φ.map f, from φ.obj c to φ.obj d, in the image whenever f ∈ S. So the arrow set is exactly the image of S under φ. Closure under inverses follows from φ.map (f⁻¹) = (φ.map f)⁻¹. Closure under composition uses injectivity on objects to identify the middle objects upstairs (if φ.obj b = φ.obj b' then b = b'), so f ≫ g exists, lies in S, and maps to the composite. Injectivity is needed: without it the plain image is in general not closed under composition. This matches the standard treatment (e.g. Brown, Topology and Groupoids), and the library proves map ⊣ comap as a Galois connection (galoisConnection_map_comap). The hypothesis is required by the construction, so the definition is not too narrow.
